scope: This file defines the machine: the console hardware, the jobs its FPGA performs and the behaviour its BIOS exposes. Implementations of the machine are the physical console, the HTML5 emulator's machine model and the Analogue Pocket core. Emulator-only features (ROM hack maker, MSX porting tools, Lab composite, merge report, the app's Debug tab, filters, FM dual-run capture, save states) are not part of the machine and are listed separately in MasterDrive_v7_Reconciliation.md.

glossary.register_banks: The VDP register-write command byte is 10bbnnnn. "bank1 R3" means register 3 of bank 1, written with bb = 01. Banks 1-3 are reachable only while XRB is set.
glossary.XRB: Extended Register Banks: Feature Enable A (bank 0 R15) bit 5. While it is clear, bits 5-4 of a register-write command are ignored as on stock hardware, and the bank 1-3 registers keep their values but have no effect (Feature Enable B and C read as 0 to the hardware). One exception: the window layer (Feature Enable A bit 2) reads its tilemap base from bank 1 R0 whether or not XRB is set (open question Q29).
glossary.Feature_Enable_A_B_C: The three opt-in registers: A = bank 0 R15, B = bank 1 R2, C = bank 1 R7. All 0 at reset.
glossary.TH_TR: Controller-port pins: TR is button 2; TH is the light-gun / multiplexing line. Both can be outputs, set through port $3F.
glossary.ESAT: Extended Sprite Attribute Table: per-sprite flip, priority, size, magnification, early clock and palette.
glossary.unique_cell: A mode with 1024 tiles, so every cell of the 32x24 screen can have its own tile.
glossary.AEL: Auto-Enhancement Layer: the optional boosts for stock software (see enhancement_layer).
glossary.bus_synchroniser: FPGA logic that holds the CPU (Z80 WAIT) until the VDP can accept an access, or the FM chip a write, needed when turbo runs the CPU faster than those chips.
glossary.SDSC: A debug-console convention used by Master System homebrew (ports $FC/$FD).

v7_changes: Port $00 is decoded in MasterDrive mode as well as Game Gear mode. v6 said GG mode only, but the Golden Axe conversion plan reverts Ax Battler's GG2SMS Start patch and relies on the stock $00 read, and the emulator already decoded it in both modes. Format corrected: bits 5-0 read 0 (the emulator returned 1s, so bit 5 reported PAL).
Ports $01-$05 (Game Gear serial/EXT link) listed explicitly for GG and MasterDrive modes; v6 named the serial link under input.multiplayer but gave no ports.
$3E bit 2 scope specified: controller decode only; not on Game Gear; not $F2 or MasterDrive's $F0-$FF.

Read values of the MasterDrive registers inside $07-$16 and $F0-$FA specified. The emulator answered every read in $07-$16 from the controller mirror, so the math result, slot readback and multitap detection could not be read.

Debug unit port reads: in the stock modes $FB-$FF read as on the stock machine (the controller mirror; $FF on the Game Gear), and the debug unit answers reads only in MasterDrive mode, which therefore decodes $F0-$FF fully. Writes reach the debug unit in every mode, as before. The emulator answered $FB-$FD reads in every mode, so stock software reading its pads at those mirror addresses saw the debug status instead.

The emulator indexed entries by byte address while advancing the address per byte, so sequential writes filled every other entry; and in Game Gear mode it treated each byte as an SMS 6-bit colour, which gave every GG title wrong colours.
