v5_changes: SG-series capability recovery: features the TMS9918 had and the SMS/GG Mode 4 VDP dropped are restored.
Enhanced legacy modes - TMS modes 0-3 may draw from 12-bit CRAM instead of the fixed TMS palette, with the sprite-per-line limit raised and line interrupts available.
16x16 sprites RE-ATTRIBUTED to the TMS9918/SG-1000, which had them before the Master System removed them. 32x32 via magnification added.
Per-sprite early clock and per-sprite magnification added (SG had per-sprite early clock; the SMS has only a global 8-pixel shift).
Extended Sprite Attribute Table widened to 2 bytes per sprite to carry the new flags.
Text window: the window layer may render as a 40-column, 6-pixel-wide text plane, bringing SC-3000 text density into Mode 4.
1024-tile unique-cell mode, recovering the Graphics II pseudo-bitmap capability at Mode 4 colour depth.
SC-3000 keyboard support through the expansion port.
New Feature Enable C register at bank 1 R7.

sg_capability_analysis.premise: The Mode 4 VDP is not a strict superset of the TMS9918. The Master System added Mode 4 and kept the legacy modes for compatibility, but several TMS capabilities have no Mode 4 equivalent.

lost_and_recovered.tms: SAT attribute bit 7 shifts that sprite 32 px left
lost_and_recovered.mode4: reg0 bit 3 shifts ALL sprites 8 px

lost_and_recovered.tms: Mode 2: 768 patterns = every one of 32x24 cells unique (pseudo-bitmap)
lost_and_recovered.mode4: 512 tiles max, so cells must be reused

lost_and_recovered.tms: SC-3000 was a computer with a full keyboard

deliberately_not_taken.reason: Mode 4 already allows 8, and MasterDrive allows 16. The TMS limit is strictly worse.
TMS sprites carry one colour each; Mode 4 sprites are 15-colour. Per-sprite colour selection is instead provided by the ESAT palette index, which gives both.
Replaced by 12-bit CRAM. The enhanced legacy modes keep the TMS structure but draw programmable colours.

detection.offset_note: The BIOS checks all three in turn; 8 KB and 16 KB ROMs carry the header lower down. v5 listed only 0x7FF0, under which every small ROM reads as headerless.
detection.bios_rule: The machine's BIOS reads the header and picks the machine to launch (bios.identification).

layout.+12..+13: product code, BCD, last four digits, high pair in the second byte
layout.+14: high nibble any remaining product digits, low nibble version
layout.+15: high nibble region, low nibble checksum range (commonly called the ROM size code)

detection.export_bios_note: An export SMS BIOS rejects any cartridge whose region nibble is not 4 with a software error. Region 8 software therefore will not boot on stock export hardware.

cpu.clock_standards: base_clock_hz is the NTSC clock. In PAL the CPU runs at pal_clock_hz, as on a PAL Master System, so a 313-line frame of 228 cycles per line is 49.70 Hz (at the NTSC clock it would be 50.16 Hz).
cpu.reset_state: After a cold reset the CPU starts in the BIOS (bios.cold_reset); software gets it from the BIOS's launch (bios.launch). At hand-over to software: PC $0000, SP $DFF0 (where the Master System BIOS leaves it), interrupts disabled (IFF1 = IFF2 = 0), interrupt mode 0, I and R 0 (as a Z80 reset sets them), AF $FFFF (as real Z80s come out of reset, though Zilog does not document it) and AF' $FFFF (a Z80 reset leaves it; the BIOS sets it); software selects IM 1 itself. BC, DE, HL, IX, IY, BC', DE' and HL' are 0: a Z80 reset leaves them, and the BIOS clears them before its launch. The emulator and the Pocket core also set SP and AF' in their CPU reset; how the console reaches SP $DFF0 is open question Q32.

turbo.principle: extra CPU cycles per frame; VDP/PSG/FM stay at 1x
turbo.clock_generation: FPGA PLL generates true 4.47/5.37/6.26/7.16 MHz at the NTSC clock and 4.434/5.320/6.207/7.094 MHz at the PAL clock: each step is the same percentage of the base clock in both standards (open question Q22, decided by the owner); VDP, PSG and FM stay at 1x
turbo.enable: Feature Enable A bit 6 - off at reset. A write to $F3 takes effect only while it is set, so unmodified SMS/GG software can never change the clock; the step stays in force until $F3 is written again.
turbo.cartridge_wait: A 250 ns cartridge ROM is fast enough up to 175 %; at 200 %, in PAL as in NTSC, every read from the cartridge or card slot ($0000-$BFFF; not the SF-7000's RAM and IPL, nor the BIOS ROM, bios.rom) takes one wait state, a halted CPU's M1 reads included (open question Q12, decided by the owner: kept). Code run from cartridge ROM therefore gains little at 200 % over 175 %; code in work RAM runs at the full 200 %. Whether cartridge writes take it too is open question Q25.
turbo.v5_error: v5 placed this on port 0x3F bits 6-4, which are the TR output levels for controller ports A and B. Any title driving TR would have changed the clock.
turbo.fm_writes: The FM chip stays at 1x. At turbo steps above 100 % the bus synchroniser holds the CPU on a write to $F0/$F1 until 12 base cycles have passed since an address write, or 84 since a data write (audio.fm.write_timing), so software written for 100 % keeps its FM music. Open question Q21, decided by the owner.

bus_synchroniser.purpose: Holds the CPU until the VDP reaches a safe access point, and holds an FM write until the FM chip can take it (cpu.turbo.fm_writes), since the CPU clock is decoupled from the VDP and the FM chip under turbo.
bus_synchroniser.source: Official Sega Mark III software reference manual
bus_synchroniser.consequence: An OUTI loop of 16 T-states is free in VBLANK at any turbo step. During active video every access waits; at 200% the steady-state penalty is 42 CPU cycles per access.

height_selection.standard: M2 (R0 bit 1) enables the extra heights. With M4 and M2 set, M1 (R1 bit 4) gives 224 lines and M3 (R1 bit 3) gives 240; with both M1 and M3 set it stays 192 lines. With M2 clear, Mode 4 is 192 lines whatever M1 and M3 say. M4 is R0 bit 2.
height_selection.masterdrive: additionally selectable through Feature Enable B bits 7-6
height_selection.note: Extra height modes are SMS2 features; they do not work on an SMS1. The name table becomes 32x32 rather than 32x28, and 0xD0 stops acting as a sprite-list terminator.
height_selection.v6_error: v6 gave 224 = M4 M3 M1 with M2 clear and 240 = M4 M3 M2 with M1 clear, swapping the roles of M2 and M3. Under it, the usual R0 = $36 with R1 bit 4 set stayed at 192 lines, and R0 = $04 with R1 bits 4-3 set gave 224 lines where hardware shows 192.

modes.0: Graphics I - 32x24 tiles, colour per 8-tile group
modes.1: Text - 40 columns of 6-pixel characters, no sprites
modes.2: Graphics II - 768 unique patterns, colour per 8x1 row (pseudo-bitmap)

legacy_modes.selection: Graphics I with none of M1-M3 set, Text with M1 (R1 bit 4), Graphics II with M2 (R0 bit 1), Multicolor with M3 (R1 bit 3); M4 (R0 bit 2) selects Mode 4. Several of M1-M3 together: open question Q19.

cram_colour.effect: The 16 fixed TMS palette entries are replaced by CRAM entries 0-15, giving 12-bit programmable colour from a 4096-colour space while the mode's tile and colour-table structure is unchanged.
cram_colour.purpose: This is to SG-1000 software what the Mode 4 hybrid is to SMS software: the same picture structure, freed from a fixed palette. An SG-1000 conversion gains full colour authority without touching its graphics layout.
cram_colour.default: off - legacy modes use the authentic fixed TMS palette

sprite_limit.effect: raises the legacy per-scanline sprite limit from 4 to the Mode 4 limit in force (8 or 16)
sprite_limit.purpose: the TMS 4-sprite limit is the single worst constraint in SG-1000 software

line_interrupts.effect: VDP register 10 line interrupts, an SMS addition, while running legacy modes (proposed in v5)
line_interrupts.purpose: raster splits and mid-screen effects in SG-1000-structured software
line_interrupts.enable: R0 bit 4, as in Mode 4, in MasterDrive mode (open question Q15, decided by the owner). In the stock machine modes the TMS modes raise none, as on the TMS9918.

legacy_modes.tables: Base addresses as on the SG-1000: name table R2 x $400, colour table R3 x $40, pattern table R4 x $800, sprite attributes R5 x $80, sprite patterns R6 x $800. In Graphics II, R4 bit 2 and R3 bit 7 pick the half of VRAM for the pattern and colour tables, and R4 bits 1-0 and R3 bits 6-0 mask the pattern and colour index, so the thirds of the screen can share tables.
legacy_modes.transparency: Colour 0 is transparent in every TMS mode, Text and Multicolor included: the backdrop (R7 bits 3-0) shows through.
legacy_modes.sprites: 32 sprites of 4 bytes (Y, X, pattern, attribute: bit 7 early clock, 32 pixels left; bits 3-0 colour), 8x8 or 16x16 (R1 bit 1), magnified by R1 bit 0; none in Text mode. At 192 lines Y = $D0 ends the list, and a sprite starts on line Y+1, or Y+1-256 when Y+1 is 225 or more (Gearsystem: 224; the two differ only for Y = $DF, off a 192-line screen either way); at 224 and 240 lines see taller_heights. Four per line as stock. When sprites overlap, the lowest-numbered is drawn on top. A transparent sprite counts towards the limit but draws nothing; neither implementation lets it take part in collisions, as in Gearsystem, and whether it should is open question Q18.
legacy_modes.status_flags: Status bit 6 is set by a fifth sprite on a displayed line, and status bit 5 when pixels of two drawn sprites meet on the screen; both when the line is drawn, not at the Mode 4 event times. What status bits 4-0 read is open question Q18.

taller_heights.enable: Feature Enable B bits 7-6 (vdp_registers.feature_enable_b_height) in MasterDrive mode, whichever picture mode is selected (open question Q17, decided by the owner). In the stock machine modes the TMS modes stay at 192 lines: the M1/M3 height selection needs M4.
taller_heights.name_table: continues below row 23: 28 or 30 rows of 32 names in Graphics I, Graphics II and Multicolor (896 or 960 bytes), of 40 in Text (1,120 or 1,200 bytes, past the 1 KB that R2 places)
taller_heights.graphics_ii: rows 24-29 take their patterns and colours from a fourth bank, as rows 0-23 take them from the first three: the bank number is the character row / 8, masked by R4 bits 1-0 and R3 bits 6-5 like the others, so with both masks fully set the fourth bank is at the pattern and colour bases + $1800
taller_heights.graphics_i_multicolor: Graphics I keeps its colour table (one byte per 8 patterns); Multicolor rows continue the four-row cycle through each pattern's 8 bytes (row & 3)
taller_heights.sprites: Y = $D0 no longer ends the list, and a sprite starts on line Y+1, or Y+1-256 when Y+1 is 241 or more, as in Mode 4; the sprite limit and flags work on every displayed line
taller_heights.timing: as Mode 4 at the same height: the frame interrupt flag at line height + 1 and the line counter on lines 0 to height (stock_behaviour.vdp)
taller_heights.vram: the tables stay in the first 16 KB of VRAM, as on the SG-1000

legacy_modes.source: TMS9918A Data Manual (Texas Instruments); Gearsystem (Video.cpp, RenderBackgroundTMS9918 and RenderSpritesTMS9918), which the emulator matches on the Pocket core's TMS test ROMs

sprites.size_16x16_source: TMS9918 / SG-1000 - present on the SG series, removed on the Master System, restored here

early_clock.per_sprite: ESAT byte 0 bit 5 - shifts that sprite 32 pixels left
early_clock.global: register 0 bit 3 - shifts all sprites 8 pixels left, unchanged
early_clock.purpose: lets individual sprites enter and leave the left edge smoothly; the SMS could only shift the whole sprite plane

esat.v5_change: widened from 1 byte to 2 to carry magnify and early clock. The v4 single-byte layout is superseded, and no bit selects it: Feature Enable C bit 4, which did, is retired (open question Q13, decided by the owner).

collision.extended: OPEN (Q28): per-sprite hit bitmaps at the bank 1 R6 base are named, but not defined, and neither implementation writes them

window_layer.tilemap: 32 x 32 entries of 2 bytes in the Mode 4 name-table format, at bank 1 R0. The window does not scroll: the cell at screen row r, column c shows entry (r, c). It replaces the background in its area, priority bits included, and sprites are drawn over it as over the background.

text_mode.effect: the window plane renders as 40 columns of 6-pixel-wide characters instead of 32 columns of 8-pixel tiles
text_mode.colours: bank1 R9 - bits 3-0 foreground palette index, bits 7-4 background palette index
text_mode.purpose: 25 percent more text per line for dialogue, menus and status panels, while the main playfield stays in Mode 4 with scrolling, sprites and 12-bit colour. Recovers SC-3000 text density without a whole-screen mode change.
text_mode.layout: its 40-column name table is at bank 1 R0 too, 40 bytes a row, row 0 at the window's top edge; the window area is filled with the background colour, then the characters are drawn from its left edge; each pattern byte is one row of a character: bits 7-2 are its six pixels, bit 7 leftmost, and bits 1-0 are not drawn

window_layer.enable: Feature Enable A bit 2, MasterDrive mode
window_layer.area: screen x from bank 0 R13 to the right edge, on the lines bank 0 R14 selects (above its split, or from the split down)
window_layer.open: open question Q29: the tile and text windows count their rows differently, the window can only lie right of the X split, and the window reads its tilemap base (bank 1 R0) even while XRB is clear

unique_cell_mode.effect: name table bit 15 becomes tile index bit 9, giving 1024 tiles - enough for all 32x24 = 768 screen cells to be unique
unique_cell_mode.trade: the extended-palette index narrows from 4 bits to 3 (8 palettes instead of 16) because bit 15 is reassigned
unique_cell_mode.source: TMS9918 Mode 2, whose 768 unique patterns made every cell independent
unique_cell_mode.purpose: recovers the Graphics II pseudo-bitmap capability at Mode 4 colour depth: full-screen unique imagery with 16-colour tiles instead of two colours per 8x1 row

line_h_table.format: one byte per line: on line y the background's horizontal scroll is the byte at base + y, in place of R8, the horizontal scroll register. The top two rows that R0 bit 6 exempts stay unscrolled.

line_v_table.format: one byte per line: on line y the byte at base + y is added to the vertical scroll (R9), modulo 256; screen x 192 and right, which R0 bit 7 exempts (stock_behaviour.vdp.v_scroll), stay unscrolled.

color_system.legacy_mode_use: With bank1 R7 bit 0 set, TMS modes index CRAM entries 0-15 in place of the fixed TMS palette.

power_on_state.cold_reset: not defined: a cold reset need not clear CRAM (the Pocket core's does not, the emulator's does); the BIOS clears entries 0-31 before its launch (bios.hand_over_memory)
power_on_state.launch: entries kept as the BIOS left them; the palette-written flags cleared
power_on_state.palette_written_flags: 16 flags; an unwritten palette aliases to palette (index AND 1)

native.addressing: Byte-addressed as on the Game Gear: a write to an even CRAM address is held in a latch and the write to the following odd address stores both bytes of the entry (entry = address >> 1). 64 bytes for 32 entries; 512 bytes for 256 entries when extended CRAM is on.

color_system.game_gear_mode: Game Gear mode uses the native byte-addressed scheme over 64 bytes.

bank_0.0-10: stock SMS VDP, including the M1-M4 mode bits
bank_0.11: Line-Scroll (H) Table Base: bits 5-0 = VRAM address >> 8 (video.scroll.line_h_table)
bank_0.12: Extended Sprite Attribute Table Base: bits 5-0 = VRAM address >> 8 (128 bytes, video.sprites.esat)
bank_0.13: Window X Split: bits 4-0 = the first window column; the window covers screen x from 8 x the value to the right edge (video.window_layer); bits 7-5 reserved
bank_0.14: Window Y Split: bits 4-0 = the split row (8 lines each); bit 7 set: the window covers the lines above the split, clear: the lines from the split down; bits 6-5 reserved
bank_0.15: Feature Enable A - bit0 CRAM native, bit1 line-scroll H, bit2 window, bit3 ESAT, bit4 16 sprites/line, bit5 XRB, bit6 turbo (enables writes to $F3), bit7 the MasterDrive I/O registers at $01-$17 (port_map.native_gate)

vdp_registers.bank_0_scope: Registers 11-15 take effect only in MasterDrive mode; in the other modes they are ignored, as on the stock VDP.
vdp_registers.bank_0_evidence: Evidence, not proof (a risk from Technical Reference v2 that v3 keeps): six commercial titles were checked and none write VDP registers 11-15, where Feature Enable A lives. It matters for old code running in MasterDrive mode, the only mode in which those registers take effect (bank_0_scope): an old title that set R15 bit 7 there would also open the I/O registers at $01-$17 (port_map.native_gate).

bank_1.0: Window Tilemap Base: bits 5-0 = VRAM address >> 8 (video.window_layer)
bank_1.1: Line V-Offset Table Base: bits 5-0 = VRAM address >> 8 (video.scroll.line_v_table)
bank_1.2: Feature Enable B - bit0 line V-offset, bit1 extended CRAM, bit2 16x16 sprites, bit3 per-sprite collision, bit4 VRAM banking, bits7-6 display height
bank_1.4: Render Bank Assignment: OPEN, no implementation defines it (open question Q28)
bank_1.5: Sprite Palette Base: OPEN, no implementation defines it (open question Q28)
bank_1.6: Collision Result Base: OPEN, no implementation defines it (open question Q28)

bits.0: Legacy modes draw from CRAM (12-bit colour in TMS modes)
bits.1: Legacy sprite limit raised from 4 to the Mode 4 limit
bits.4: reserved (it selected a 2-byte ESAT; retired, since the ESAT is always 2 bytes per sprite: Q13)

bank_1.8: Text Window Pattern Base - bits 5-0 = VRAM base >> 8
bank_1.9: Text Window Colours - bits 3-0 foreground palette index, bits 7-4 background

power_on_values.note: Display is OFF at power-on: R1 0xA0 has no display-enable bit. R2 0xFF puts the screen map at 0x3800, R5 0xFF the sprite table at 0x3F00, R6 0xFB the patterns in the first 8 KB.
power_on_values.others: At a cold reset and at the launch (bios.launch) bank 0 R11-R15 and every bank 1-3 register are 0, as are $09, $0B, the math unit ($0C-$10) and the DMA registers ($F4-$FA); R0-R10 take the values above

vdp_registers.xrb_semantics: Extended Register Banks: Feature Enable A (bank 0 R15) bit 5. While it is clear, bits 5-4 of a register-write command are ignored as on stock hardware, and the bank 1-3 registers keep their values but have no effect (Feature Enable B and C read as 0 to the hardware). One exception: the window layer (Feature Enable A bit 2) reads its tilemap base from bank 1 R0 whether or not XRB is set (open question Q29).
vdp_registers.feature_enable_b_height: Feature Enable B bits 7-6: 00 = height from the mode bits, 01 = 224 lines, 10 = 240 lines, 11 = reserved (192). A 224/240 selection by the mode bits takes precedence.

input.controller: Genesis 3-button, TH multiplexed. 0xDC carries port A buttons plus port B up/down; 0xDD carries port B buttons, Reset, CONT and both TH readbacks.

keyboard.enable: Feature Enable C bit 5 on MasterDrive; always live in SG-1000 (keyboard attached), SC-3000 and SF-7000 modes

ports.0xDC: PPI port A, input, 8 bits of matrix data
ports.0xDD: PPI port B, input, matrix data in bits 3-0; bits 7,6,5 read 0,1,1 with nothing attached
ports.0xDE: PPI port C, output, row select in bits 2-0 via a 74LS145; bit 3 cassette out; bits 5-7 printer
ports.0xDF: PPI control; not readable, always returns 0xFF

keyboard.polarity: Taken as active low with pull-ups - a pressed key reads 0, an unused matrix position always reads 1. Evidence, not proof: this rests on a single source that contradicts itself (a risk from Technical Reference v2 that v3 keeps). Both implementations use it.
keyboard.rows: 8 groups: rows 0-6 keyboard, row 7 the two gamepads
keyboard.port_c_readback: Reading port C returns its output latch: the last value written, or 0 after a mode word.
keyboard.ghosting: The matrix has no diodes. Two or more keys held on one row make any key on another row sharing those columns read as pressed, and the transpose holds for columns. Real behaviour; modelled and toggleable.
keyboard.common_init: Software writes 0x92 to the control register and 0x07 to port C, configuring A and B as inputs with port C output and selecting row 7 for the gamepads.
keyboard.reset_key: One key raises an NMI on the Z80 rather than appearing in the matrix
keyboard.v5_error: v5 specified row select on port 0x3F bits 2-0 with data on 0xDC bits 6-0 and 0xDD bit 0. That scheme does not exist on hardware.
keyboard.reset_state: The 8255 resets with every port an input. Port C's pull-ups then select row 7, the pads, so SG-1000 software that never touches the PPI still reads its controllers with the keyboard attached.
keyboard.mode_word: Writing a mode word (bit 7 set) to $DF clears the output latches, so port C selects row 0 until software writes it; with bit 7 clear the write sets or clears one port C bit (bit set/reset). Intel 8255A behaviour.

port_3F.bits_7_4: TH/TR output levels: 7 = port B TH, 6 = port B TR, 5 = port A TH, 4 = port A TR
port_3F.bits_3_0: data direction, 1 = input, 0 = output: 3 = port B TH, 2 = port B TR, 1 = port A TH, 0 = port A TR
port_3F.reset_state: 0xFF: every pin an input (bits 3-0 set), level bits 7-4 set
port_3F.region_detection: With TH configured as an output, an export machine reads back the level driven; a Japanese machine always reads 0. This is how software detects region.

mega_drive_mouse.interface: TH-clocked serial on the controller port
mega_drive_mouse.sequence: 4 ID nibbles (0,B,F,F), then sign/overflow, buttons, and two bytes of delta

sports_pad_trackball.interface: TH-clocked, strobe on 0x3F bit 5 for player 1 or bit 7 for player 2
sports_pad_trackball.reports: two 8-bit absolute counters that wrap from 0xFF to 0x00 - not deltas
sports_pad_trackball.sequence: X7-X4 strobe low, X3-X0 strobe high, Y7-Y4 strobe low, Y3-Y0 strobe high
sports_pad_trackball.data: port A bits 3-0, with buttons S1 and S2 on bits 4 and 5
sports_pad_trackball.direction: right increases X, up increases Y
sports_pad_trackball.source: Official Sega Mark III manual, trackball section

pointing_devices.purpose: Computer mode is a mouse and keyboard GUI; the pointer is drawn as a hardware sprite at no per-frame cost
pointing_devices.note: Both share one driver with two device profiles, detected by response pattern.

input.stock_mapping: In the stock modes (Master System, Game Gear, SG-1000, SC-3000) the console presents its Mega Drive pad as that machine's controller: A is button 1 (TL), B is button 2 (TR), and Start is the Game Gear's Start, or the Pause button on the Master System, SG-1000 and SC-3000 (enhancement_layer start_pause, on at power-on). C is used only by the auto-fire boost. A Mega Drive pad plugged into a Master System gives B and C as buttons 1 and 2; the console uses A and B so that the pad's first two buttons are the old consoles' two. MasterDrive software reads the pad as a Mega Drive pad (controller). Decided by the owner, October 2026.

audio_control.write: $F2 bits 1-0 select which sound chips are heard: 0 the PSG only (the power-on state), 1 the FM chip only, 2 neither, 3 both
audio_control.read: $F2 returns bits 1-0 of the last value written (bits 7-5 carry a C-sync counter on the Japanese SMS; MasterDrive returns 0 there)
audio_control.detection: Software disables the I/O chip ($3E bit 2) before reading $F2 so the controller decode does not drive the bus; the FM latch must still answer.
audio_control.source: MAME sms_m.cpp (smsj_audio_control_r, smsj_set_audio_control); Gearsystem (Audio.h) does the same for Japanese consoles

fm.level: OPEN: the balance of FM and PSG on the original (open question Q20). Both implementations make one FM channel at full volume peak at half a PSG channel at full volume.
fm.write_timing: After an address write to $F0 the chip needs 12 master-clock (base) cycles before the data; after a data write to $F1, 84 before the next write (YM2413 Application Manual). Software leaves this time itself at 100 %; at turbo the bus synchroniser holds the CPU until it has passed (cpu.turbo.fm_writes).

ports.0x07: data (write): one unsigned 8-bit sample, 128 = silence, queued in the FIFO
ports.0x08: control (write): bits 1-0 the sample rate, 0 = 8,000, 1 = 11,025, 2 = 16,000, 3 = 22,050 samples a second; bits 7-2 reserved. Read: the fill (fill_readback)

pcm.fill_readback: $08 read: bits 6-4 = bytes queued / 8, saturating at 7 (56-64 bytes read 7); the other bits read 0. A write to $07 while 64 bytes are queued is dropped. Decided by the owner (open question Q14).
pcm.output: mono, on both sides; while the FIFO is empty the output holds the last sample, and reset returns it to silence. How the rates are made from the machine clock, and the level beside the PSG, are open question Q27.

wavetable.waveform: 32 samples of 4 bits per voice (8 is the centre), written through $11 and $12

register_layout.0x11: bit 5 selects the voice (0 or 1) that $11-$15 address; bits 4-0 the waveform position $12 writes; bits 7-6 reserved
register_layout.0x12: bits 3-0 the sample at that position (the position does not advance); bits 7-4 ignored
register_layout.0x14: bits 3-0 frequency, high 4 bits; bit 7 key on (1 plays, 0 silences); bits 6-4 reserved
register_layout.0x15: bits 3-0 volume, 0 silent to 15 full, linear; bits 5-4 the sides it is heard on (bit 5 left, bit 4 right; both at reset); bits 7-6 reserved

wavetable.pitch: A voice with frequency f (12 bits, 0 silent) plays its 32-sample waveform; how f maps to a pitch, and the level beside the PSG, are open question Q27.

cartridge_slot.sega_mapper_reach: 8-bit bank registers address 256 x 16 KB = 4 MB, the largest cartridge ROM the machine takes (open question Q2, decided by the owner).

dual_slot.source_select: $09 bit 0 set: $4000-$7FFF reads the card, bank $0B; bit 1 set: $8000-$BFFF the same (cartridge RAM mapped by $FFFC bit 3 comes first); clear: the cartridge, banked by its mapper. $09 acts only with a Sega-mapper cartridge: with the Codemasters, Korean and Korean MSX mappers $4000-$BFFF reads the cartridge whatever $09 holds. $0000-$3FFF is always the cartridge, except while the BIOS ROM is mapped (bios.rom). Bits 7-2 are kept and read back but do nothing. It acts only with a card inserted, in MasterDrive mode. How $09 relates to the slot enables in $3E is open question Q30.
dual_slot.card_bank: $0B bits 4-0: one of 32 banks of 16 KB (512 KB) of the card; reads back

sg1000_carts.mapping: linear, no mapper, 1 KB work RAM mirrored from 0xC000
sg1000_carts.note: SG-1000 and SC-3000 cartridges run natively. The BIOS starts a headerless cartridge of 64 KB or less as SG-1000 software where the platform knows its size (bios.identification, Q31); SC-3000 software is chosen in the BIOS's Machine item or the platform's machine setting.

sega.fffc_bits: 7 ROM-write enable, 4 RAM enable 0xC000-0xFFFF, 3 RAM enable 0x8000-0xBFFF, 2 RAM bank select, 1-0 bank shift
sega.slot_0_protection: the first 1 KB is unaffected by banking, preserving the interrupt vectors
sega.cart_ram: 32 KB in two banks of 16 KB, as the 315-5235 maps them: $FFFC bit 3 maps cartridge RAM over $8000-$BFFF and bit 2 selects the bank (open question Q3, decided by the owner; memory.cartridge_ram). Bits 7, 4 and 1-0 of $FFFC are implemented by neither implementation.

codemasters.registers: 0x0000, 0x4000, 0x8000 exactly (Gearsystem and MAME decode the full address)
codemasters.no_vector_protection: the first 1 KB banks too, so interrupt vectors must be replaced
codemasters.on_cart_ram: high bit written to 0x4000 maps 8 KB at 0xA000-0xBFFF (Ernie Els Golf)
codemasters.note: no RAM mirroring of mapper writes, so the last value cannot be read back
codemasters.v6_error: v6 said any address within a slot acts as its register. No source supports it; with it, a write into the on-cart RAM window's slot would also bank-switch.

korean.registers: 0xA000 exactly selects slot 2; slots 0 and 1 fixed to banks 0 and 1

msx_nemesis.nemesis_variant: last 8 KB bank fixed at 0x0000, second at 0x2000
msx_nemesis.implementation: The emulator and the Pocket core implement the MSX variant only; the Nemesis variant is not implemented yet.

mappers.note: Only a Sega-mapper cartridge has hardware at 0xFFFC-0xFFFF. On the other families those addresses are plain work RAM and must not bank anything.

sc3000_carts.rom: 0x0000-0x7FFF; a smaller ROM repeats through the range (both implementations take the address modulo its length; Q39)
sc3000_carts.cart_ram: 0x8000-0xBFFF, 16 KB; or 32 KB contiguous 0x8000-0xFFFF with work RAM disabled
sc3000_carts.work_ram: 2 KB only, mirrored every 2 KB across 0xC000-0xFFFF
sc3000_carts.verified_software: Sega Home BASIC v1.0j, Mitec SC-3000 BASIC Level 2 and Level 3 all boot and poll the keyboard
sc3000_carts.v5_error: v5 folded SC-3000 into the SG-1000 map with 1 KB of work RAM and nothing at 0x8000. No 32 KB SC-3000 BASIC can initialise under that map.

sf7000.rom_overlay: With /ROM SEL low the IPL is mapped over 0x0000-0x3FFF, mirrored from 8 KB, but WRITES to that range still land in RAM. Reads see ROM, writes see RAM.

ppi.0xE4: port A, input: FDC and printer status
ppi.0xE6: port C, output: FDD, FDC, ROM mapping, printer
ppi.0xE7: control; /ROM SEL is driven by 8255 bit set/reset, not whole-port writes

sf7000.port_c_bits: 0 FDD /INUSE, 1 FDD /MOTOR ON, 2 FDC TC, 3 FDC RESET, 6 /ROM SEL, 7 printer /STROBE

floppy.geometry: 40 tracks x 16 sectors x 256 bytes = 160 KB
floppy.owner: FPGA, backed by disk images rather than a drive
floppy.rationale: A harvested uPD765 would still need a 3-inch drive and 3-inch media, both scarcer than the controller. Images have no mechanism to fail and are what survives in preservation.

sf7000.source: SF-7000 IPL disassembly; register map and bit assignments are documented, not inferred
sf7000.ppi_mode_word: As on the keyboard PPI, a mode word clears port C, which drives /ROM SEL low and maps the IPL back in.

media.other_media: Decided by the owner (Q2): the console also reads the media of its computer side, SC-3000 cassettes and SF-7000 disks. How it reads them (in which modes, through which ports, and whether the boot menu loads an image or software reads the signal) is open question Q23.

dma.registers: 0xF4-0xFA, MasterDrive mode (fully decoded like 0xF0-0xF3, so not behind the I/O gate)

register_layout.0xF4: source address, low byte; in fill mode, the fill byte
register_layout.0xF6: bits 1-0 the source of a memory transfer: 0 the CPU address space ($0000-$FFFF as the CPU reads it: the BIOS ROM while it is mapped, with no wait state on its bytes, bios.rom), 1 the card (card bank $0B, source address bits 13-0), 2 work RAM (the selected 8 KB bank, address bits 12-0), 3 reserved; bits 3-2 the mode: 0 memory to VRAM or CRAM, 1 VRAM to VRAM, 2 fill, 3 reserved; bits 7-4 reserved
register_layout.0xF8: bits 5-0 destination address, high bits (a transfer starts in VRAM $0000-$3FFF); bit 6 set: the destination is CRAM (address bits 8-0, its 512 bytes); bit 7 reserved
register_layout.0xFA: bits 5-0 length, high bits (a length of 0 means 16,384 bytes); bit 7 written as 1 starts the transfer; bit 6 reserved

dma.behaviour: A transfer moves length bytes, source and destination each counting up by one. A VRAM destination counts on past $3FFF into the upper 16 KB (address bits 14-0), and VRAM to VRAM reads source address bits 14-0, whether or not VRAM expansion is on. The registers keep what was written (the addresses do not advance) and read back at $F4-$FA. A transfer to CRAM stores the bytes as CRAM holds them (the Game Gear 12-bit format, two bytes per entry, whatever the CRAM write mode) and marks each palette it writes as written (color_system.power_on_state).
dma.timing: OPEN (Q26): the emulator completes a transfer at once and charges the CPU one T-state per byte, plus, for a transfer from the CPU address space, the cartridge wait state (cpu.turbo.cartridge_wait) on each byte it reads from $0000-$BFFF at 200 %, whatever the display is doing.

registers.0x0F: result low: the product low byte, or the quotient
registers.0x10: result high: the product high byte, or the remainder

math_unit.divide: A / B, unsigned: the quotient in $0F, the remainder in $10. A divide by zero gives $FF in $0F and $00 in $10, which 255 / 1 also gives, so software that must tell them apart tests B. Decided by the owner (open question Q7).

compatibility.reset_state: At hand-over to software (the BIOS's launch): all features disabled, turbo at 100%, legacy modes authentic; behaviour identical to stock hardware in every mode. A cold reset starts the machine's BIOS in MasterDrive mode instead (bios.cold_reset).
compatibility.extension_gating: Feature Enable A, B and C; the extended register file behind XRB.
compatibility.sg_software: An unmodified SG-1000 ROM renders with the fixed TMS palette, 4 sprites per line and no line interrupts, exactly as on real hardware, until Feature Enable C bits 0-1 are set. MasterDrive software in a legacy mode gets line interrupts with R0 bit 4 (video.legacy_modes.enhancements.line_interrupts).

implementation_order: 1. CRAM expansion and dual write mode
4. Dual-slot loader, port 0x09, card bank at 0x0B
7. ESAT 2-byte: flip, priority, size, magnify, early clock, palette
9. Window layer, then text window mode
10. Line H and V offset tables, 224/240 heights
11. Legacy mode enhancements: CRAM colour, raised sprite limit, line interrupts (R0 bit 4 in MasterDrive mode), the 224/240-line heights
13. PCM FIFO, math unit, per-sprite collision
14. Multitap protocols, EXT serial link, SC-3000 keyboard
15. TIER 2: extended CRAM, wavetable, VRAM banking, unique-cell mode
17. Card battery SRAM, banked work RAM, lint mode, debugger views
v6_changes: Turbo control moved off port 0x3F. Bits 6-4 there are the TR output levels on real hardware: stock SMS/GG software driving TR would have silently changed the clock, and MasterDrive software could never have used both. Turbo is now port 0xF3, gated by Feature Enable A bit 6, outside the 0x00-0x3F mirror range.

Keyboard interface corrected. The SK-1100 is read through the 8255 PPI at 0xDC-0xDF, not via port 0x3F as v5 stated. Row select is PPI port C bits 2-0 at 0xDE; data returns on port A (0xDC, 8 bits) and port B (0xDD, bits 3-0). The v5 scheme does not exist on hardware and real SC-3000 software would not have worked with it.
Full SK-1100 matrix behaviour specified, resolving the v5 note that it must be transcribed during implementation.
Work RAM raised from 8 KB banked to 128 KB in 16 banks of 8 KB, to host SF-7000 compatibility and give native software real headroom.

SC-3000 promoted to its own machine mode. It is not the SG-1000: the cartridge sets the memory map, work RAM is 2 KB mirrored, and the cart supplies RAM at 0x8000. v5 folded it into the SG-1000 map, under which no SC-3000 BASIC can run.
SF-7000 expansion added: 64 KB RAM, 8 KB IPL ROM with a read/write-split overlay, second PPI at 0xE4-0xE7, uPD765-class floppy controller at 0xE0-0xE1.
Bus synchroniser cadence set to the official figures: 16 Z80 T-states in VBLANK, 29 during active video.
Pointing devices added: Mega Drive mouse and Sports Pad trackball, both TH-clocked on the controller port.
Cartridge mapper families specified: Sega, Codemasters, Korean, MSX/Nemesis.
VDP power-on register values specified from the official manual.
Port map conflict with the 0x3E/0x3F mirror scheme documented as an open risk.
Port 0x3E memory enables implemented rather than merely stored. The emulator kept the value and ignored all six bits, so joystick, RAM, cartridge and card disables had no effect.

Display height selection corrected in the emulator to match what this profile already specified: the M1-M4 mode bits in registers 0 and 1. The emulator had only the MasterDrive Feature Enable B path, so no SMS or GG title could reach the 224 or 240-line modes. The profile was right and the implementation was not.

Debug facility ports remapped to avoid colliding with the SDSC debug console at 0xFC-0xFD, an established SMS homebrew convention. The FPGA UART now implements SDSC, so existing homebrew debug output works unchanged. FPGA control moved to 0xFB and the watchpoint register file to 0xFE/0xFF.

work_ram.bank_readback: $0A reads the selected bank in bits 3-0; bits 7-4 read 0. Decided by the owner (open question Q9), so an interrupt handler can save and restore the bank.
work_ram.rationale: 128 KB lets the first 64 KB be presented as a contiguous bank set for SF-7000 compatibility, and gives native software real headroom. v5 specified 8 KB banked to 64 KB.
work_ram.stock_compatibility: Bank 0 at reset presents the stock 8 KB an SMS title expects.

vram.expansion_enable: Feature Enable B (bank1 R2) bit 4 enables the 32 KB map; bank1 R3 bit 0 selects the bank the CPU port reaches

cartridge_ram.control: $FFFC bit 3 maps it, bit 2 selects the bank (media.mappers.sega.cart_ram)
cartridge_ram.save_card: a save-card profile holds the first 8 KB of bank 0 (open question Q24)

port_3E_memory_enables.bit_3: 0 enable the base 8 KB BIOS ROM, the machine's own (bios.rom)
port_3E_memory_enables.reset_value: 0xE0 at a cold reset: the BIOS ROM, RAM and controllers enabled; cartridge, card and external port disabled (bios.cold_reset). 0xA8 when the BIOS launches a game: the state of a machine whose BIOS has handed over to a cartridge - cartridge, RAM and controllers enabled; BIOS, card and external port disabled (bios.launch)

bios.what: The machine's own start-up program: Z80 software in the 8 KB BIOS ROM, written for this project (bios/ in the repository, MIT licence; no Sega code, logo or wording). It shows a menu before every game; holding Start while switching on skips the menu. Decided by the owner, 16 October 2026: a full menu before every game, the same on the console, the emulator and the Analogue Pocket core; both the BIOS menu and a platform's own settings menu set the machine and the boosts, the last change winning; the menu waits for PLAY.
bios.cold_reset: Switching on; on the platforms also Reset, a new cartridge, and a change of the machine or video setting. Every block takes its reset value, except that the machine starts in MasterDrive mode with $3E = 0xE0 (BIOS ROM, work RAM and controllers enabled; cartridge, card and external port disabled). The CPU starts at $0000, in the BIOS (cpu.reset_state).
bios.rom: 8 KB, at $0000-$BFFF (repeated every 8 KB) while $3E bit 3 is clear and bit 6 set. With bits 3 and 6 both clear the cartridge answers, so software that writes $3E = 0x04 (bit 2 set, disabling the I/O chip before it reads $F2, audio.fm.audio_control.detection, and the other bits clear) keeps running from its own ROM. BIOS reads, the CPU's or a DMA transfer's from source 0, take no cartridge wait state (cpu.turbo.cartridge_wait). The BIOS writes nothing below $C000. What $3E bit 3 does after the launch is open question Q36.
bios.header_read: The BIOS copies a short routine to work RAM, which sets $3E to 0xA8 (cartridge on, BIOS off), copies the 16 bytes at $7FF0, $3FF0 or $1FF0 (machine.detection) and sets $3E back to 0xE0, as the Master System BIOS does. After a cold reset every mapper has ROM offsets $0000-$7FFF at those addresses.

ports.scope: MasterDrive mode, while the BIOS ROM is mapped ($3E bit 3 clear, bit 6 set). Otherwise $18-$1F are the $3E/$3F mirrors (port_map.mirror_scheme).
ports.0x19: read/write: the setting at the index; the index then steps by one
ports.0x1F: write 0xA5: launch the game (bios.launch); other values do nothing; reads 0xFF

settings.0: the machine to launch: 0 Master System, 1 Game Gear, 2 SG-1000, 3 SC-3000, 4 SF-7000, 5 MasterDrive. After a cold reset the platform's choice (16) if the platform runs that machine (21), otherwise 0. A write of a machine the platform does not run (21), or of a larger value, is ignored
settings.1-9: the boosts for the next launch, in enhancement_layer.boosts's order: sprite limit, stock overflow flag, Start = Pause, turbo step (0-4), VRAM speed-up, auto-fire, pseudo-stereo, Game Gear uncrop, True TMS colours. Index 4 ignores values above 4; the others keep bit 0
settings.16: read only: the platform's machine choice, 0xFF for none (Auto)
settings.17: read only: bit 0 a cartridge is inserted, bit 1 a card is inserted, bit 2 the platform has USB, bit 3 PAL video, bit 4 the platform has its own settings menu
settings.18: read only: the cartridge's size as log2 of its byte count, rounded up (13 = 8 KB, 22 = 4 MB); 0 if unknown (Q31)
settings.19: read only: the platform's mapper setting (0 Sega, 1 Codemasters, 2 Korean, 3 Korean MSX), 0xFF if unknown
settings.20: read only: the region, 0 export, 1 Japan (Q34)
settings.21: read only: the machines the platform runs, bit n for machine n

bios.boosts: Each boost has a current value, the one in effect, and a next value, for the next launch; the first cold reset after the platform starts takes the platform's own values for both. A change in a platform's own menu sets both at once, during the menu or in a game; a write to setting 1-9 sets only the next value; the launch makes the next values current. A later cold reset keeps each current value and makes it the next value too, so a change made in the BIOS menu and not yet launched is dropped. Between cold resets, whichever changed a boost last wins. The BIOS reads settings 1-9 every frame, so a platform change shows in its menu at once, and writes a boost only when the player changes it there. The machine choice lasts one launch (Q33).
bios.identification: Default machine: the platform's choice (16) when it has one (with a cartridge inserted, a choice of the SF-7000, which does not play the cartridge, counts as none); else the header's region nibble (3 or 4 Master System, 5-7 Game Gear, 8 MasterDrive, other values Master System); else, with no header, SG-1000 if the size (18) is known and 64 KB or less, otherwise Master System (Q31). The checksum is shown, never enforced: the BIOS refuses no cartridge.
bios.launch: When 0xA5 is written to $1F the CPU runs no further instruction. At the VDP's next wrap to line 0 every block is reset as at a cold reset, except that the machine is the one in setting 0, $3E is 0xA8 and the boosts' next values become current. Memory is not touched: VRAM, CRAM, work RAM and cartridge RAM stay as the BIOS left them, and so do the CPU registers a Z80 reset does not set. Before the launch the BIOS turns the display and its interrupts off, clears VRAM $0000-$3FFF, the 32 CRAM entries and work RAM bank 0, sets AF' to 0xFFFF and clears BC, DE, HL, IX, IY, BC', DE' and HL' (bios.hand_over_memory says what it leaves). So the game finds what a direct start gives. The launch waits until the button that asked for it (Start on the skip path; from the menu both Start and B, whichever launched) has read released in two frames running, so the game does not start with it held; other buttons may stay held. The BIOS checks this before its clears, which take about seven frames: a button pressed during them is held at the launch (a Pause held so is no press, bios.pause). The launch happens at the frame wrap whichever line the $A5 write came on, and the first clock after it is that of a cold reset. How the console does this with its 315-5535 is open question Q37.
bios.hand_over_memory: At hand-over work RAM bank 0, VRAM $0000-$3FFF and CRAM entries 0-31 are zero (the BIOS clears them) and the palette-written flags are clear (the launch resets them). Work RAM banks 1-15, VRAM $4000-$7FFF, CRAM entries 32-255, the wavetable waveforms, SC-3000 cartridge RAM and the SF-7000's RAM are cleared neither by a cold reset nor by the launch: software must not assume them zero. (The emulator's cold reset clears VRAM, CRAM and the waveforms; the Pocket core's, whose memories are block RAM, does not.) Whether they should be cleared is open question Q38.
bios.pause: No Pause (NMI) from a cold reset until the launch: software cannot mask an NMI, and one during the header read would run the cartridge's handler. A Pause held through the launch (the Pause button, or Start with Start = Pause on) is no press: the game gets a Pause when it is pressed again.
bios.menu: Rows 0-2 are Mode 4 tiles (the name, the BIOS version and the device row CART, CARD, USB, SYSTEM, the current one in palette 1); rows 3-23 are the text window, 40 columns of 6-pixel characters at x 8-247, with a status line at the bottom. A sprite arrow marks the selected item. Left and right change device, up and down move, B changes an item, C goes to the top, Start plays from any device when a cartridge is inserted, or with none when the platform's choice is the SF-7000 and it runs one (setting 21), which starts from its own ROM and disks. CART: what the header says, PLAY, the machine (Auto or one the platform runs, not the SF-7000, which does not play the cartridge), the boosts (for MasterDrive software only True TMS colours, which also acts on it, Q11; a boost that does not act on the machine PLAY starts is marked "(no effect)", enhancement_layer.boosts). CARD: whether a card is inserted. USB: none on a platform without USB. SYSTEM: the BIOS version, the machine ID ($17), the video standard and region, a controller test (B starts it; every button then shows while held and none acts until Start and A are held together). The BIOS silences the PSG at start. Stock colours only, no animation; a page is drawn into the text name table not on screen and shown from a vertical blank, so a page change goes from one frame to the next. With the display on its VDP data writes are at least 29 T-states apart (cpu.bus_synchroniser). It relies on the text window counting its rows from its top edge (Q29). Not in this round, each waiting on an open question or on hardware the implementations lack: per-title settings, the save card manager, USB, computer mode, firmware update, the POST display, PLAY's region, video, controller and slot options, the SETTINGS page, the SYSTEM memory and video tests, FPGA configuration and card health, the save-restore offer at power-on, the return to the BIOS from a running game, cassettes and disks.

port_map.mirror_scheme: On SMS hardware every EVEN address 0x00-0x3E mirrors 0x3E and every ODD address 0x01-0x3F mirrors 0x3F. The Game Gear decodes 0x00-0x06 separately for its own registers. On every stock machine the PSG is written at any port in 0x40-0x7F and the VDP answers across 0x80-0xBF (even ports data, odd ports control); on the Master System and Game Gear the V counter reads at every even port and the H counter at every odd port in 0x40-0x7F. The SG-1000, SC-3000 and SF-7000 have no 0x3E/0x3F registers: in those modes writes to 0x00-0x3F do nothing.
port_map.mode_scope: In MasterDrive mode the registers at 0x01-0x17 answer only while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set (port_map.native_gate); 0x00 always answers. In Game Gear mode 0x00-0x06 are always its registers. Writes to VDP bank 0 R11-R15 take effect only in MasterDrive mode (vdp_registers.bank_0_scope). In every other case these ports and registers do what they do on the stock machine.
port_map.native_gate: Decided by the owner, October 2026 (Q1, with Q8): in MasterDrive mode the I/O registers at 0x01-0x17 answer only while software has Feature Enable A (VDP bank 0 R15) bit 7 set. Until then MasterDrive mode decodes 0x01-0x17 as the Master System does: an even port writes 0x3E, an odd port writes 0x3F, and a read returns $FF. 0x00 (Start and region) always answers. Bit 7 is clear at reset. The gate is live: clearing the bit closes the ports again, and what the registers were set to (work RAM bank, slot select, card bank, stereo, the math operands, PCM and wavetable) stays in force.
port_map.open_risk: RESOLVED by the I/O gate (Q1, native_gate). The MasterDrive registers stay at 0x01-0x17 inside the 0x3E/0x3F mirror range, and answer only once native software sets Feature Enable A bit 7, so old code running in MasterDrive mode (a retagged or converted title, or an export cartridge started in MasterDrive mode, software_detection) that writes a mirror address there reaches memory or I/O control, as on a Master System. What remains: old code that writes VDP R15 with bit 7 set opens the registers (vdp_registers.bank_0_evidence), and old code in MasterDrive mode meets the rest of MasterDrive behaviour (software_detection.native_mode).

registers.0x00: Game Gear port 0: bit 7 Start (0 = pressed), bit 6 region (1 = export), bits 5-0 read 0. Decoded in Game Gear AND MasterDrive modes; in MasterDrive mode it answers whether or not the I/O gate is open.
registers.0x06: PSG stereo panning (write-only): Game Gear mode, and MasterDrive mode while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set (port_map.native_gate)
registers.0x17: machine ID, read-only, $A7 (software_detection.machine_id): MasterDrive mode while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set (port_map.native_gate)
registers.0x18-0x1F: The BIOS's ports, MasterDrive mode while the BIOS ROM is mapped (bios.ports); otherwise the $3E/$3F mirrors
registers.0xC0-0xDF: controllers: 0xDC/0xDD, mirrored across the range; while the SK-1100 keyboard is live (input.keyboard.enable), the PPI at 0xDC-0xDF instead, mirrored across the range
registers.0xF3: turbo step - relocated from 0x3F in v6
registers.0x01-0x05: Game Gear serial / EXT link registers: Game Gear mode, and MasterDrive mode while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set (port_map.native_gate)
registers.0xFB-0xFF: debug unit (see debug_facility); reads answer only in MasterDrive mode

port_map.io_chip_disable: $3E bit 2 disables the controller decode (the $DC/$DD mirror across $C0-$FF) on the Master System and on MasterDrive. It has no effect on the Game Gear, even in SMS mode. It does not affect $F2 (FM detection) or MasterDrive's fully decoded $F0-$FF window.

masterdrive_read_values.0x01-0x17: decoded by the FPGA in MasterDrive mode while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set (port_map.native_gate): $01-$05 the Game Gear serial registers, $06 $FF (write-only), $07-$17 as below; ports with no readable register return $FF, never the controller mirror. While the gate is closed they read $FF, as on a Master System.
masterdrive_read_values.0x08: PCM FIFO fill (audio.pcm.fill_readback): bits 6-4 = bytes queued / 8, saturating at 7
masterdrive_read_values.0x0F-0x10: math result, low then high: the product, or the quotient then the remainder (math_unit.divide)
masterdrive_read_values.0xFB-0xFF: debug unit: $FB the control value as written; $FC and $FD status (bit 7 debug host attached, bit 6 set, bit 0 trace buffer full); $FE and $FF $FF

fpga_partition.principle: A real 315-5535 ASIC renders the base layer; the FPGA owns everything the ASIC has no register for. Modelling the split explicitly keeps the emulator structurally honest.
fpga_jobs: VDP control-port gating (absorbs bank>=1 writes so they cannot corrupt ASIC registers)
fpga_partition.overlay_capability: Because the FPGA sits in the CPU-to-VDP path it can hold the Z80 and draw over ANY running software, including a commercial cartridge that knows nothing about MasterDrive. This is the mechanism for save dialogs, standby, and switching between game and computer mode.

debug_facility.rationale: Four capabilities a debugger running on the Z80 cannot provide, each following from the FPGA sitting on the bus.

ports.0xFB: control: bits 1-0 trace mode, bit 2 arm watchpoint, bit 3 raise overlay, bit 4 clear trace, bit 5 emit marker
ports.0xFC: SDSC console control; value 2 clears the console
ports.0xFE: watchpoint register select bits 2-0; kind in bits 7-6 (VRAM, port, CPU write, CRAM)

debug_facility.watchpoint_fields: address low and high, range end low and high, value to match, flags (bit 0 match value, bit 1 one-shot), ignore count
debug_facility.watchpoint_note: A single address on a busy port such as 0xBE fires tens of thousands of times per second. Range, value match, ignore count and one-shot together reduce that to one meaningful hit.
debug_facility.trace_buffer: FPGA-side, mirrored to FRAM on a fault, so it outlives the crash that destroyed the program state. It is not cleared by a machine reset.
debug_facility.overlay: Composited after the ASIC output, using a font in FPGA memory. Never touches the program VRAM or CRAM, so software cannot detect it happened.
debug_facility.post: Runs before the CPU leaves reset. Ten documented codes; also blinked on the power LED for a machine that cannot reach video.
debug_facility.availability: Writes reach the debug unit in every machine mode, since its purpose is inspecting stock software; stock hardware ignores writes to $FB-$FF. Reads of $FB-$FF answer from the debug unit only in MasterDrive mode. In the stock modes they read as on the stock machine (the controller mirror; $FF on the Game Gear), because stock software may read its pads there.
debug_facility.read_values: debug unit: $FB the control value as written; $FC and $FD status (bit 7 debug host attached, bit 6 set, bit 0 trace buffer full); $FE and $FF $FF

stock_behaviour.note: Behaviour of the stock parts that every implementation must reproduce. These are not MasterDrive additions; they are listed because the emulator had them wrong until October 2026 and the Pocket core is verified against it.

cpu.halt: An interrupt taken in HALT returns to the instruction after HALT.
cpu.ei: Interrupts are not accepted until the instruction after EI has executed.
cpu.sampling: Maskable interrupts are sampled between instructions.
cpu.index_prefix: DD/FD take a displacement only for the (HL) forms. (IX+d) costs 8 T-states more than (HL); LD (IX+d),n costs 5 more. DDCB: BIT 20, others 23. A prefix followed by another prefix costs 4.

vdp.h_scroll: Screen x = map x + R8 (the background moves right as R8 increases). Latched once per line before the line is drawn; R0 bit 6 exempts rows 0-1.
vdp.v_scroll: R9 is latched once per frame; a write takes effect from the next frame. R0 bit 7 exempts screen x 192 to the right edge: the lock is by screen position, whatever the horizontal scroll (Gearsystem, Video.cpp RenderBG).
vdp.sprite_y: A sprite starts on line Y+1. When Y+1 is 241-256 it starts at Y+1-256 instead, so Y = $F0-$FF shows its lower rows at the top of the screen (Gearsystem and MAME; a plain 8-bit compare would differ only for 32-line magnified sprites at Y = $E0-$EF).
vdp.extra_height: 224/240-line modes use a 32x32 name table at (R2 bits 3-2) x $1000 + $700, the map wraps at 256 lines instead of 224, and $D0 no longer ends the sprite list.

event_timing.note: Within the 228-cycle line, these happen at fixed cycle offsets (Gearsystem's model, which passes the SMS VDP test ROMs). The machine uses the 315-5535 column.
event_timing.line_render: 195 / 186 (background of this line, sprites of the next)
event_timing.collision_flag: 20 / 22 + X x 228 / 256 of the line after the sprites were drawn, or at the render event if that comes first (Gearsystem drops such late collisions; the hardware flags a collision anywhere on the line)
event_timing.io_access_point: IN/OUT reach the port 10 T-states into the instruction (IN A,(n), OUT (n),A)

v_counter.source: Charles MacDonald, Sega Master System VDP documentation (which lists NTSC 240 as 00-FF, 00-06: 263 values for a 262-line frame; the implementations use 00-05)

vdp.h_counter: 00-93 then E9-FF, one count per two pixels; latched on a TH edge for the light gun.
vdp.frame_flag: Status bit 7 is set at cycle 25 (SMS2) / 27 (315-5535) of line height + 1, the second line after the last displayed one, and stays set until the status register is read.
vdp.line_counter: On lines 0 to height inclusive (one line past the display) the counter counts down; on reaching 0 it reloads from R10 and raises the line interrupt. On other lines it is reloaded from R10. Mode 4 only as stock (TMS modes raise no line interrupt); in MasterDrive mode the TMS modes raise it too, enabled by R0 bit 4 as in Mode 4 (Q15, decided by the owner).
vdp.line_timing: 228 CPU cycles per line, 262 lines NTSC, 313 PAL; the overrun of the last instruction of a line belongs to the next line.

psg.tone: Counters run at CPU/16 and toggle the output on reaching zero; a period of 0 behaves as 1.
psg.noise: The noise counter (rate $10/$20/$40 or tone 2) toggles a flip-flop; the 16-bit shift register advances on its rising edge, once per two counter periods. White noise taps bits 0 and 3; writing the noise register resets the register to $8000.
psg.volume: Attenuation 2 dB per step; 15 is silent.

io.low_port_reads: Reads of $00-$3F return $FF on the Master System, and on the Game Gear and MasterDrive for every port they do not decode as a register.
io.tr_readback: A TR pin configured as an output ($3F bit 0 or 2 clear) reads back the level driven: $DC bit 5 for port A, $DD bit 3 for port B.
io.game_gear_decode: Above $C0 the Game Gear answers only $C0/$DC (port A) and $C1/$DD (port B, with bits 7-6 = $3F bits 7-6); every other port reads $FF, $F2 included (no FM).
io.fm_latch: The $F2 FM detection latch answers in Master System and MasterDrive modes only.

stock_behaviour.verification: Batman Returns (Europe) SMS in PAL at frames 30, 60, 120, 200, 500, 900 and 1500, and Batman Returns (World) GG at frames 200, 500, 900 and 1500: the emulator and the Pocket core RTL (Verilator) both match Gearsystem, Game Gear within Gearsystem's colour rounding (it expands channel value 5 to 86 rather than 85). Plus VDP test ROMs at 192/224/240 lines (October 2026).

software_detection.status: RESOLVED (Q8, decided by the owner, October 2026)
software_detection.question: How does one ROM tell, at run time, that it is on a MasterDrive? Extended features are reachable only in MasterDrive mode, which the header region (8) selects, and an export SMS BIOS refuses region 8. A single ROM for both machines therefore cannot use region 8.
options: Two ROMs from one source (what the Super Mario Land DX port does now).
A boot-menu option to run a region-4 cartridge in MasterDrive mode, plus a read-only machine ID register the ROM can test.
An unlock sequence that switches a running region-4 title into MasterDrive mode.
software_detection.chosen: option 2: a boot-menu option and a read-only machine ID register
software_detection.boot_menu: The BIOS's Machine item (bios.menu) can start an export (region 4) cartridge in MasterDrive mode instead of Master System mode. It then starts as MasterDrive software does: every extension off, and the I/O registers waiting for Feature Enable A bit 7 (port_map.native_gate). The Analogue Pocket core's System setting and the emulator's machine selector choose the machine the BIOS offers first (bios.settings 16; changing it restarts the machine).
software_detection.native_mode: Old code started this way meets MasterDrive behaviour: the pad reads as a Mega Drive pad (B and C as buttons 1 and 2 with TH high), the enhancement layer does not act, 0xF0-0xFF are fully decoded, VDP registers 11-15 take effect, and the TMS modes raise line interrupts when R0 bit 4 is set. 0x00 reads Start and region. The option is for software that detects the machine; ordinary games run in Master System mode.

machine_id.encoding: high nibble $A = MasterDrive; low nibble = the machine version (7)
machine_id.access: read-only, MasterDrive mode, while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set (port_map.native_gate); a write is absorbed
machine_id.otherwise: while the gate is closed a read gives $FF and a write is a 0x3F mirror write; in the other modes the port does what it does on the stock machine ($FF on the Master System and Game Gear, the controller mirror in the SG-1000, SC-3000 and SF-7000 modes)

software_detection.procedure: Write VDP R15 with bit 7 set (on a stock VDP register 15 does nothing), then IN A,($17): a MasterDrive in MasterDrive mode answers with $A in the high nibble. Test the high nibble rather than only for a value other than $FF, since some sources describe open bus at the low ports of stock consoles.
software_detection.source: Super Mario Land DX port design, distribution question

modding.machine_side: Computer mode can apply a BPS patch to a cartridge image while writing a blank card, which is how a mod reaches real hardware. The console plays mods; it does not make them.
modding.not_machine: Making mods (the ROM hack maker and its plugins) is emulator-only.
modding.distribution: Mods are distributed only as BPS patches.
modding.source: Golden Axe / ROM hack maker work (October 2026)

enhancement_layer.purpose: Optional boosts for unmodified SG-1000, SC-3000, Master System and Game Gear software, applied by intercepting the fixed hardware interfaces (VDP ports, PSG, pads) rather than patching the ROM. Full rationale and tiers: SuperSega_AutoEnhancement_Layer.md (the "AEL doc" below), an earlier design document that is not in this repository.
enhancement_layer.default: Every boost but two is off at power-on, so the machine behaves as stock hardware: True TMS colours starts on, so SG-1000 and SC-3000 software shows the colours it was made for (Q11), and Start = Pause starts on, because the console's pad has no Pause button (input.stock_mapping). Each one is switched independently, in the BIOS menu on every platform, and also in the emulator's AEL panel and the Analogue Pocket core's settings (Interact) menu: the last change wins (bios.boosts). Off at power-on means a first start: a platform keeps the boosts in effect across a Reset, and where the console keeps them is Q33.
enhancement_layer.precedence: Explicit software intent wins. Every boost acts only on software running in the stock modes (SG-1000, SC-3000, Master System, Game Gear): MasterDrive software sets these features itself and reads C as a button of its own. Pseudo-stereo also stops once software writes $06. Start = Pause applies in the Master System, SG-1000 and SC-3000 modes (the Game Gear has a Start button of its own). The TMS colour boost is the one exception: it also acts on MasterDrive software's TMS modes (Q11).
enhancement_layer.settings: Each boost has a current value and a value for the next launch, which the BIOS menu sets; a platform's own menu sets both (bios.boosts).

boosts.sprite_limit: 16 sprites per line instead of 8 in Mode 4, and instead of 4 in the TMS modes.
boosts.overflow_stock: With the raised limit, status bit 6 is still set by a 9th sprite on a line, for software that reads it as logic. Mode 4 only: in the TMS modes it has no effect.
boosts.start_pause: Start on the pad raises the Pause NMI (SMS, SG-1000, SC-3000 modes). On at power-on.
boosts.turbo: A turbo step (125-200 %) for stock software in the SMS, GG, SG-1000 and SC-3000 modes. MasterDrive software sets its own step through $F3.
boosts.vram_boost: No VDP access wait while a turbo step is active: the bus synchroniser stops holding VDP accesses, but still holds FM writes (cpu.turbo.fm_writes).
boosts.autofire: While C is held, button 2 repeats: it toggles every two frames (15 Hz at 60 Hz). The pad state itself is not changed, so releasing C leaves button 2 as the pad has it.
boosts.pseudo_stereo: Until software writes $06, the PSG is panned tone 0 left, tone 1 right, tone 2 and noise centre (the $06 value $DE).
boosts.gg_uncrop: Game Gear software is shown at the full 256x192 instead of the 160x144 window.
boosts.tms_colour: SG-1000/SC-3000 picture modes use true TMS9918 colours instead of the Master System approximation.
boosts.fm_present: Inherent to the machine (the FM unit is always fitted), not a switch.

enhancement_layer.not_modelled: "VRAM write reliability" (AEL doc, tier 1) has no switch: the emulator and the Pocket core never drop a VDP write, so they already behave as if it were on.
enhancement_layer.region_speed: "Region speed correction" (AEL doc, tier 1) is the machine's 50/60 Hz video setting (the emulator's PAL switch, the Pocket core's Video setting), not a separate boost.

open_questions.detail: Registers $06-$16 sit in the $3E/$3F mirror range, a risk for old code running in MasterDrive mode that writes a mirror address there. Decided by the owner in October 2026: the registers stay, and in MasterDrive mode $01-$17 answer only while Feature Enable A bit 7 is set; until then those ports are the $3E/$3F mirrors and read $FF, and $00 still answers (port_map.native_gate).

open_questions.topic: Maximum ROM size and mapper layout above 4 MB
open_questions.detail: The slot was specified for 8 MB, which needs a ninth bank bit. Decided by the owner in October 2026: 4 MB, the stock bank registers' reach (media.cartridge_slot.sega_mapper_reach); the console also reads the media of the computer side (media.other_media).
Decided by the owner in October 2026: 32 KB, two banks of 16 KB as the 315-5235 maps them (memory.cartridge_ram, media.mappers.sega.cart_ram).

open_questions.topic: ESAT entry format; H-flip per sprite or per tile
open_questions.detail: 2 bytes per sprite; byte 0 bit 1 H-flip, bit 0 V-flip, per sprite.

open_questions.topic: Unique-cell mode and 32 KB VRAM: coupled or independent
open_questions.detail: Coupled: unique-cell mode requires VRAM expansion (Feature Enable B bit 4).
Off at reset. A title enables it itself (Feature Enable A bit 6, then $F3). The enhancement layer's turbo boost is for unmodified software in the stock modes and does not apply to MasterDrive titles.
The emulator computed ((A << 8) | B) / B. Decided by the owner in October 2026: A / B, the quotient in $0F and the remainder in $10, $FF/$00 for a divide by zero (math_unit.divide).

Decided by the owner in October 2026: a boot-menu option runs an export cartridge in MasterDrive mode, and a read-only machine ID register at $17 reads $A7, behind the I/O gate of Q1 (software_detection).

$0A was write-only, so an interrupt handler that switches banks could not restore the previous one. Decided by the owner in October 2026: $0A reads the selected bank in bits 3-0 (memory.work_ram.bank_readback).
A hack-maker workflow, not a machine question; listed so it is not lost.

open_questions.topic: Default of the TMS colour boost
open_questions.detail: Decided by the owner in October 2026: true TMS9918 colours are on at power-on, one of the two boosts that start on (Start = Pause is the other), and the boost also acts on the TMS modes of MasterDrive software. The emulator already did both; the Pocket core does the same.

cpu.turbo.cartridge_wait gives one wait state per cartridge read at 200 % (250 ns ROM); the emulator applied it only with its cartridge-timing setting and the Pocket core not at all. Decided by the owner in October 2026: kept, and the Pocket core adds it. Both implementations now apply it.

ESAT has been 2 bytes per sprite since v5, and v6 confirmed it (Q4), but Feature Enable C bit 4 still selected a 2-byte mode and the emulator implemented a 1-byte layout when it was clear. Decided by the owner in October 2026: the bit is retired (reserved) and the ESAT is always 2 bytes per sprite; the emulator no longer has the 1-byte layout.

$08 bits 6-4 report the fill of a 64-byte FIFO, which three bits cannot encode: the emulator returned the fill modulo 8, so a full FIFO read as empty. Decided by the owner in October 2026: bits 6-4 = bytes queued / 8, saturating at 7 (audio.pcm.fill_readback).

open_questions.topic: Line interrupts in the TMS9918 (legacy) modes
open_questions.detail: v5 made line interrupts in the legacy modes a MasterDrive enhancement (video.legacy_modes.enhancements.line_interrupts), but no enable bit was ever assigned; as stock, TMS modes raise none (stock_behaviour.vdp.line_counter). Decided by the owner in October 2026: in MasterDrive mode the line counter runs in the TMS modes and R0 bit 4 enables the interrupt, as in Mode 4; the stock modes stay as stock. Both implementations already did this.

open_questions.topic: Register layouts defined only by the emulator
open_questions.detail: The bit layouts of the DMA engine ($F4-$FA), PCM control ($08 write), the wavetable ($11-$15), slot select ($09), the VDP base registers (bank 0 R11 and R12, bank 1 R0, R1, R5 and R6) and the window split (bank 0 R13 and R14) are defined today only by the emulator's implementation (the Pocket core already follows it for $09). They need writing into the profile and the Technical Reference, and checking, before the Pocket core implements them, as v7 did for the math unit. Decided by the owner in October 2026: the emulator's layouts are adopted (dma.register_layout, audio.pcm, audio.wavetable, media.dual_slot, vdp_registers, video.scroll, video.window_layer), with four clear faults fixed. What the emulator does not settle is open: Q26 to Q30.

open_questions.topic: Feature Enable B height in the TMS modes
open_questions.detail: Feature Enable B bits 7-6 select 224 or 240 lines for MasterDrive software, but the documents defined the heights only for Mode 4, while both implementations also applied them in the TMS9918 modes. Decided by the owner in October 2026: they apply in the TMS modes, which extend their tables below line 192 (video.legacy_modes.taller_heights): the name table continues, Graphics II takes rows 24-29 from a fourth pattern and colour bank, and $D0 no longer ends the sprite list.

open_questions.topic: TMS-mode status bits 4-0 and transparent sprites
open_questions.detail: Two details of the sprite flags in the TMS modes are not settled for this VDP. (1) What status bits 4-0 read: the TMS9918A puts the number of the fifth sprite there; Gearsystem does that whenever a TMS mode is selected (not on the Game Gear) and reads $1F in Mode 4; the Pocket core reads $1F and the emulator 0 in every mode. (2) Whether a transparent (colour 0) sprite takes part in collisions: the TMS9918A Data Manual says it does; Gearsystem, the emulator and the Pocket core leave it out.

open_questions.topic: Several TMS mode bits set at once
open_questions.detail: The implementations take M2 (Graphics II) first, then M1 (Text), then M3 (Multicolor); Gearsystem takes M1, then M3, then M2; on the TMS9918A such combinations give undocumented hybrid modes. Which picture should the machine show?

How loud the FM chip is beside the PSG on the original Japanese Master System, where the two are mixed in analogue, is not known: MAME gives both chips the same gain, Gearsystem lowers the PSG to 0.8 while both play, and neither cites a measurement. Both implementations make one FM channel at full volume peak at half a PSG channel at full volume. The chip also has separate melody and rhythm outputs, whose mix on the console's board is not known either; the Pocket core uses IKAOPLL's default weights (2 and 3), and the emulator has no rhythm instruments. What balance should the machine have?

The YM2413 needs 12 master-clock cycles after an address write and 84 after a data write before it takes the next write. Software written for 100 % spaces its writes by CPU time, so at turbo steps above 100 % they can come too close: on the Pocket core a test driver that leaves the chip little more than the minimum at 100 % played no FM at 200 %. Decided by the owner in October 2026: at turbo the bus synchroniser holds the CPU on a write to $F0/$F1 until the chip can take it, as it does for the VDP (cpu.turbo.fm_writes). Both implementations do this.

The turbo steps were defined only at the NTSC clock: 4.47, 5.37, 6.26 and 7.16 MHz. Decided by the owner in October 2026: in PAL they are the same percentages of the PAL clock, 4.434, 5.320, 6.207 and 7.094 MHz (cpu.turbo.clock_generation). Both implementations already did this, because their turbo is a multiple of the base clock.

The owner decided that the console reads SC-3000 cassettes and SF-7000 disks (Q2, media.other_media). In which modes, through which ports, and whether the boot menu loads an image or software reads the signal (and whether it writes them) is not defined. The SF-7000 floppy controller exists in SF-7000 mode; neither implementation reads cassettes.

open_questions.topic: The save card: game identity and profile size
open_questions.detail: A save-card profile holds the first 8 KB of bank 0 of a game's cartridge RAM, which is 32 KB (Q3), and each card entry carries a 32-bit game ID that the machine does not define (the emulator derives it from a sampled hash of the ROM, so two ROMs of the same size that differ only between sampled bytes share their card saves). Should a profile hold all 32 KB, and what identifies a game: a CRC-32 of the whole ROM, the header's product code, version and region (SG-1000 and SC-3000 cartridges have no header), or something else? How do existing cards carry over?

The cartridge wait state at 200 % (Q12, cpu.turbo.cartridge_wait) applies to reads, which a 250 ns ROM limits; both implementations apply it to reads only. Should writes to the cartridge slot (cartridge RAM at $8000-$BFFF, mapper registers) take it too?

The emulator completes a DMA transfer as soon as $FA bit 7 is written and charges the CPU one T-state per byte (with the cartridge wait state on bytes read from the cartridge at 200 %), whatever the display is doing, and the bus synchroniser does not take part (dma.timing). How long should a transfer take, does the CPU wait for it, and may it write VRAM during the active display? Also, the destination register reaches only $0000-$3FFF, but a transfer counts on into the upper 16 KB, even without VRAM expansion: should it wrap at $3FFF, follow bank 1 R3, or have a fifteenth address bit?

open_questions.topic: PCM and wavetable clocks and levels
open_questions.detail: The PCM rates (8,000, 11,025, 16,000 and 22,050 samples a second) and the wavetable's pitch (the emulator plays a voice's waveform f x 3.2 times a second) are not made from the machine clock; none of the four rates is a whole fraction of the 3.579545 MHz clock. And their level beside the PSG and the FM chip is the emulator's choice: PCM at full scale peaks at 0.2 of the output's full scale, a wavetable voice at full volume at 0.12, a PSG channel at full volume at 0.16. Which clocks and levels should the machine have, and does $F2 mute them?

open_questions.topic: Render bank, sprite palette base, collision result base and per-sprite collision
open_questions.detail: Bank 1 R4 (render bank assignment), R5 (sprite palette base) and R6 (collision result base), and Feature Enable B bit 3 (per-sprite collision, which is meant to write hit bitmaps at the R6 base, video.sprites.collision) are named in the documents, but neither implementation does anything with them, so their layouts and behaviour are not defined. What do they hold?

The tile window reads its tilemap by screen row, so a window from row 20 down starts at tilemap row 20, while the text window counts its rows from the window's top edge. And R14 bit 7 picks the side of the Y split, but R13 has no side bit, so the window can only lie right of the X split. And the window reads its tilemap base, bank 1 R0, even while XRB is clear, when the bank 1 registers are otherwise without effect. Which row rule should both use, should the window be able to lie left of the X split, and should its tilemap base need XRB? The BIOS's menu relies on the text window's rule (bios.menu): settling it the other way changes the BIOS too.

open_questions.topic: Slot select and the $3E slot enables
open_questions.detail: $09 maps the card into $4000-$BFFF by itself (media.dual_slot). On the stock Master System, $3E bit 5 enables the card slot and bit 6 the cartridge slot. The emulator ignores bit 5, and ignores bit 6 whenever a card is inserted; the Pocket core decodes $09 and $0B but loads no card. How should $09 and $3E bits 5-6 combine, and what does $0000-$3FFF read when $3E disables the cartridge?

open_questions.topic: Identifying a headerless cartridge on the console
open_questions.detail: Without a TMR SEGA header the BIOS takes a cartridge of 64 KB or less as SG-1000 software, otherwise as Master System software (bios.identification). That needs the size, which the Pocket core and the emulator know from the file but a console cannot read from a cartridge (setting 18 reads 0), so on the console Auto plays every headerless cartridge as Master System software. How should the console tell SG-1000 and SC-3000 cartridges, and headerless Japanese Master System ones, apart?

open_questions.topic: How the console holds and starts its BIOS
open_questions.detail: The owner's plans keep the BIOS in SPI flash, which the Z80 cannot run from, so the console's FPGA must present it as the 8 KB BIOS ROM (from block RAM, say). And a Z80 reset leaves SP at $FFFF on real parts, not the hand-over $DFF0 (cpu.reset_state), which the emulator and the Pocket core set in their reset (the BIOS sets AF' itself). How does the console's launch reach that state: does the FPGA give the CPU a few instructions (LD SP,$DFF0; JP $0000) after the reset, or something else?

open_questions.topic: Where the console keeps the BIOS's choices
open_questions.detail: A platform with its own settings menu keeps the boosts the BIOS sets until they change again (bios.boosts); the console has no such menu. Where does it keep them (the plans' FRAM, per title or for all)? And the BIOS's machine choice lasts one launch: should it outlast a Reset, as the boosts do?

The Pocket core and the emulator have a region setting (export or Japan), which the BIOS reads (setting 20) and which port $00 bit 6 and the TH read-back follow. The documents do not say which region the console is, or whether it has a switch.

The BIOS ROM is 8 KB, as the Master System's base BIOS ROM behind $3E bit 3, and the menu uses about half of it. The owner's plans add a save card manager, USB import and export and a computer mode, which will not fit: should the BIOS ROM grow, be paged (and through which register), or should those tools live elsewhere?

Both implementations keep the BIOS ROM reachable after the launch: in Master System, Game Gear and MasterDrive modes, a $3E write with bit 3 clear and bit 6 set maps it over $0000-$BFFF again, and in MasterDrive mode the BIOS's ports answer too, so software could start another machine with $A5 at $1F. On the stock machines the BIOS behind bit 3 is the Master System's own (the Game Gear maps only $0000-$03FF). Should the MasterDrive BIOS stay reachable after the launch, in which modes, and should its launch port then work?

The launch resets every block at the VDP's wrap to line 0, so that the first clock after it is that of a cold reset (bios.launch). The Pocket core does this in its own logic and the emulator at a frame boundary. On the console the VDP and PSG are inside the 315-5535: can the FPGA reset them at that moment, or must it rewrite their registers, and how does the raster's phase come out?

open_questions.topic: Memory the BIOS does not clear
open_questions.detail: Work RAM banks 1-15, VRAM $4000-$7FFF, CRAM entries 32-255, the wavetable waveforms, SC-3000 cartridge RAM and the SF-7000's RAM keep what they held across a cold reset and the launch, so a game can find what an earlier game left (bios.hand_over_memory); the emulator's cold reset clears VRAM, CRAM and the waveforms. Should a cold reset or the launch clear them, and should both implementations then do the same?

A cartridge image need not be a power of two long. Reads beyond it inside the cartridge's address range wrap into the image in both implementations (the address taken modulo the image's length), except in the emulator's SG-1000 mode, which reads 0xFF there and never mirrors; the Pocket core mirrors a power-of-two image through its size in every mode. On a real cartridge it depends on how the board decodes the address. What should a read beyond a cartridge's ROM return, in each mode?
